transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-07-21 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Dr. Anna Patel (CISO - Crestview), Mark Rivera (VP Engineering - Crestview), Jasmine Li (Cloud Architect - Crestview)
Recording id: ff-20270721-crestview-01

Auto-generated summary: Discussed pilot scope focused on security/compliance requirements and benchmarking. Notes on next steps and artifacts to share.

[00:00] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Liam from Redwood, AE on this account, and with me is Sofia, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Dr. Anna: Good, thanks. Busy day, appreciate you taking the time.
[00:18] Mark: Hi all, Mark here. We'll try to keep it focused, we've got a pretty tight security review window.
[00:26] Sofia: Great, we'll keep it tight. The goal today is to align on success criteria for the POC, the workload shape and sizing, and most importantly your security/compliance blockers — SOC 2, ISO, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, that sort of thing.
[00:42] Jasmine: Yep that's right. We're trying to validate a pilot for clinical note summarization, so data is PHI-adjacent and the security bar is high.
[00:50] Liam: Understood. Quick run-through of what a typical Redwood pilot looks like: 4-6 week engagement, we run a small reserved cluster or hosted with VPC peering depending on your needs, we run benchmarks against your sample payloads, and we validate operational concerns like latency, cost, and auditability.
[01:10] Dr. Anna: A couple of top-line asks: we need SOC 2 Type II evidence or equivalent, an ISO 27001 statement of applicability, and we need to understand how SSO/SAML will work with your console for access control. Also audit logs retention is a hard ask — 7 years for some teams, but for pilot maybe 12 months?
[01:30] Sofia: Right — we can provide a SOC 2 summary and our ISO posture. For full Type II artifacts we can share redacted reports and controls mapping. On SSO, we support SAML and OIDC; we can provision SAML metadata and you can map groups to roles via RBAC. The console audit logs and API-level logs can be exported to your SIEM via syslog or pushed to an S3 bucket — retention is configurable.
[01:54] Mark: When you say logs, do you log request/response bodies? That's a no for us unless it's redacted.
[02:00] Sofia: Good callout. By default we capture operational metadata — timestamps, request ids, model used, latency, token counts. Request/response payloads are not stored unless configured; we have an option for encrypted log archival for debugging — typically that's enabled only with customer consent and can be redacted or piped through your KMS.
[02:20] Jasmine: So KMS integration — do you support customer-managed keys? We need keys we control for encrypting any persisted data.
[02:26] Liam: Yes, we offer KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM options for Private deployments. For hosted pilots we can do a bring-your-own-key flow where the key is used for storage encryption and snapshots.
[02:39] Dr. Anna: Can you show how RBAC maps to our SAML groups?
[02:44] Sofia: Sure. You can map SAML attributes to Redwood roles — admin, operator, viewer — and then operators can only run benchmarks, viewers see dashboards, etc. We can also create scoped API keys tied to a role and TTL.
[03:02] Mark: On the operational side, we need latency targets: our acceptance criteria is 95th percentile under 500ms for 1-2k QPS? Is that realistic for a pilot?
[03:14] Sofia: 1-2k QPS is a lot for a pilot. Typical pilot is 10-50 QPS to validate correctness and latency. If you want to test throughput we can stand up dedicated capacity. For latency, sub-500ms at 95th depends on model size and prompt length — with smaller models and quantized weights it's achievable, with large-generation workloads we'll see higher tail latency.
[03:38] Dr. Anna: For clinical summarization our prompts average 700 tokens input with 200 token outputs. We expect medium latency, but consistency matters more than absolute speed.
[03:50] Sofia: That helps. For that shape we recommend a dedicated small GPU pool and we can run our KV/prefix caching to improve perf for repeated prompt templates. We'll need a sample of typical prompts to size memory.
[04:06] Liam: For success criteria let's capture both qualitative and quantitative: a) model accuracy/quality on your eval set — target F1 / ROUGE thresholds you define, b) latency at 95th percentile under your pilot QPS, c) auditability — logs and access controls meeting your compliance team signoff, and d) integration work such as SSO with SAML + KMS key exchange.
[04:28] Mark: Sounds good. Timeline? We have a compliance window end of August so ideally POC complete by mid-August.
[04:36] Liam: Tight but doable. If we start next week we can do a 4-week POC: week 1 infra + SSO + keys, week 2 benchmarking and model tuning, week 3 iterate on quality, week 4 handoff and docs. Does that align?
[04:50] Dr. Anna: Yes. But legal will need to review the SOC/ISO artifacts before we start spinning infra.
[04:58] Liam: We can share the redacted SOC 2 summary and ISO checklist immediately after this call.
[05:05] Jasmine: One question on private deployments: if we want on-prem later, what does the network topology look like? VPC peering, private endpoint?
[05:13] Sofia: For Private we offer a customer-managed control plane with connectors. For cloud we're typically VPC peering or PrivateLink; for on-prem we'd ship an air-gapped package or use an appliance model. For the pilot we recommend VPC peering to keep setup simple.
[05:28] Mark: Data residency — logs that contain PHI can't leave our region. Can you guarantee region mapping?
[05:35] Liam: Yes, you can pin cluster regions and we can ensure storage is in region. For hosted with dedicated capacity we can provision capacity in your chosen cloud region.
[05:44] Dr. Anna: About audit logs — need to know fields captured and retention policy. Also chain of custody: who had access during troubleshooting?
[05:54] Sofia: We'll provide an audit log schema. Fields include timestamp, actor, resource, action, request id, model identifier, and ancillary metadata. Access to logs is restricted via RBAC and only Red- wood SREs access logs for debugging under a controlled, recorded escalation process — we'll provide a runbook for that.
[06:18] (brief crosstalk)
[06:28] Mark: On benchmarking: what metrics will you measure out-of-the-box?
[06:33] Sofia: Latency (p50/p95), tokens-per-second, cost-per-1k-tokens, model quality metrics you provide (e.g., ROUGE, BLEU, custom heuristics), error rates, and request success/failure rates. We'll also track concurrency and memory usage.
[06:51] Dr. Anna: For quality we'll run your eval set and want reproducible runs. Can we pin model versions?
[06:58] Liam: Yes, you can pin model versions and we support rollouts and canary tests. We also store model version metadata in the audit trail.
[07:06] Jasmine: How do you handle PII/PHI redaction during logging for debugging?
[07:11] Sofia: We can configure automatic redaction rules and tokenization before persisting logs. Alternatively, we can stream logs to your S3 bucket and you can apply your own transformations under your KMS.
[07:26] Dr. Anna: Any third-party subprocessors we should know about?
[07:29] Liam: We list subprocessors in our security documentation — typical ones are cloud providers (AWS/GCP), monitoring providers, and identity providers. We'll provide the full list in the package.
[07:40] Mark: Ok let's talk acceptance pass/fail: who signs off? Security/CISO plus engineering?
[07:47] Dr. Anna: Security sign-off is mandatory for pilot success. Engineering sign-off for integration and perf. If both approve, we consider pilot passed.
[07:56] Sofia: We'll prepare an acceptance checklist with owners.
[08:02] (5 minute jump; mid-call)
transcript_continued:
[32:10] Sofia: Running through bench plan — we'll need a 1k-sample of typical prompts and a 100-sample heavy tail set to stress cache misses. Can you provide that by Friday?
[32:22] Jasmine: Yes we can, we'll scrub PHI and provide synthetic equivalents where necessary.
[32:29] Liam: Great. On the KMS exchange we'll need a contact in your security team to coordinate key rotations.
[32:36] Dr. Anna: That's me, Anna. We'll provide the proper key policies.
[32:41] Mark: For the SAML metadata we'll need a service provider config from you.
[32:45] Sofia: We'll send the SP metadata and an integration guide.
[32:50] (brief pause)
[33:05] Dr. Anna: One more ask: can you provide an example of an audit log export with redaction to confirm it meets legal requirements?
[33:12] Liam: Yes, we'll provide a sample export and a mapping doc.
[33:18] Jasmine: About timelines earlier — if we need a dedicated pool for scale tests, how long to provision?
[33:24] Sofia: For dedicated capacity typically 48-72 hours to provision if GPUs are available; if it's cross-region or special skus it may take longer. For a quick pilot we'll start with hosted with reserved nodes.
[33:37] Mark: Ok. On cost modeling we'll need an estimate for the pilot: where's the cost driver? Model size vs token volume?
[33:44] Sofia: Both. Model size drives GPU-hours and memory; prompt length and output length drive token counts. We'll provide an estimated token cost and reserved cluster hourly rate so you can forecast.
[33:58] Dr. Anna: For the SOC 2 artefacts, will you share control narratives mapping to our ISMS?
[34:04] Liam: We'll share a controls mapping doc that maps Redwood controls to your control framework.
[34:10] Jasmine: Will support teams be under NDA for access to logs?
[34:14] Liam: Yes, all Red- wood employees that require access are under NDAs and we can provide list of personnel if needed.
[34:21] Mark: Any blockers we haven't covered?
[34:24] Dr. Anna: Just legal reviewing docs — if those pass, we can move quickly.
[34:29] Liam: Ok action items recap: I'll send SOC/ISO summaries and security deck; Sofia will share benchmarks and SP metadata; Jasmine will provide samples. We'll aim to start infra next week pending legal.
[34:46] (closing)
[34:48] Dr. Anna: Thanks everyone.
[34:51] Mark: Thanks.
[34:53] Sofia: Thanks, we'll follow up with the attachments.
[35:00] Liam: Appreciate it, talk soon.
